name: Sulfacarbamide

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Germany, first in 1988 — for liver harm and blood problems

similar.name: Sulfathiazole
problems: Pulled from the market in United States and 2 other countries, first in 1970 — for kidney harm, liver harm and serious skin reactions

similar.name: Sulfamethazine
problems: Pulled from the market in Germany, first in 1992

summary: Sulfacarbamide was pulled from the market in Germany in 1988 due to blood problems and harm to the liver [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, the drug received a high risk score of 94 for the liver and a low score of 12 for the heart [M]. Similar medicines have also been removed from the market, such as Sulfathiazole, which was taken off shelves in the United States and two other countries for causing kidney harm, liver harm, and serious skin reactions [4]. Another similar drug, Sulfamethazine, was pulled from the market in Germany in 1992 [5].
